To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the presence of native species in cities is important for biodiversity; 2) the size of green spaces is important for biodiversity, but the importance of size depends on species; 3) the heterogeneity of green spaces is associated with greater abundance of some bird species; 4) the management of green spaces is an important factor for some bird and butterfly species; and 5) proximity to natural habitats is important for many species.
the presence of native species and habitat heterogeneity in green infrastructure are important features for biodiversity conservation in cities.

understanding how green infrastructure and urban biodiversity interact.
understanding and promoting biodiversity in cities.
how green infrastructure and nature in urban landscapes can be planned and designed in a way that maximises the benefits of ecosystem services, while minimising the costs to society.

green infrastructure is a good way to increase biodiversity in cities.

biodiversity in urban areas is not a lost cause and there are many opportunities to increase biodiversity.
